BTW, "export \(.key)=\(.value)" has serious security problems. Always use the @sh filter in jq to shell-quote strings before dumping them into a context where they'll be evaluated as code.
...you don't want "description": "Prevent users from injecting $(rm -rf ~) or '$(rm -rf ~)' into commands" to actually run rm -rf ~
Beyond that, declare export doesn't make sense. If you want everything to be exported, make it declare -x -- take out the export.

When I do that, all text (even english) is rtl and the arabic words in my kableExtra tables still read ltr @tarleb

from the pandoc MANUAL: "For bidirectional documents, native pandoc spans and divs with the dir attribute (value rtl or ltr) can be used to override the base direction in some output formats." So try e.g. [hello world]{dir=rtl}

Add the keep_tex: true option to the output format, and look at the .tex file that is produced. Figure out how to modify that file to get the text you want. If you know LaTeX and have worked with Arabic in it before, that should be easy. If not, you're going to need LaTeX help -- see tex.stackexchange.com. Once you have the .tex file corrected, you can use the strings it contains in your tables, and produce the table with escape = FALSE, so those strings are transmitted as-is to the final output. If this all works, please post an answer to your question for others to see.
For an old description of the LaTeX approach, see here: tex.stackexchange.com/q/12347
